turn_text: A lot of what we see about Congress, the 24-hour news networks, it's very partisan. It doesn't really portray, I think, the human side of Congress. And you're there, you see them every day, good, bad, or otherwise. When you peel that partisan layer away, how representative being the house of representatives, is this of America as a whole?

Yeah, I think that one thing we don't focus enough on, whether it was in Frankfurt or now in Washington, is how many people in these bodies actually get along. That doesn't get likes on Twitter. That doesn't get people to tune in on the cable news networks when you're talking about how people can get along and how they can agree. The word collegial sounds too formal almost, but I think there's a lot of members who do have friendships with people from all over the country, from all across the political spectrum. It's a very representative body where we've got people, literally every person who lives in the United States of America has a member of Congress. There's 435 of us from all different walks of life. And we share a common bond, you know, we share a common bond that we're serving in the House of Representatives. And maybe it's just because I'm optimistic, maybe it's because I'm new, maybe it's because it's both, right? But I really do believe that the majority of people who serve in a legislative body, whether again, it's a state legislature or in the United States Congress, they're doing it. for the right reasons. They're doing it because they want their community, their state, our country to be a little bit better than how we found it. And so I find it's easy to strike up conversations with most people. Now, there are some people, you know, if you get 435 people together from anywhere, right, go to any place of employment and get 435 people who work there. I think unfortunately now some of those people are getting a lot more oxygen and amplification through social media and through some of the news networks who are looking for ratings.
